newsitem.title: USA: Fran dumps heavy rain as it moves across Virginia.
newsitem.headline: Fran dumps heavy rain as it moves across Virginia.

text.p: Tropical Storm Fran dumped heavy rain Friday as it moved inland across Virginia, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the storm's center was at latitude 37.3 north and longitude 79.1 west, near Lynchburg, Va., moving north-northwest near 16 mph (26 kmh), National Hurricane Center said.
A gradual turn toward the north and deceleration was expected during the next 24 hours, increasing the risk of flooding in some areas.

Maximum sustained winds were near 40 mph (64 kh), with higher gusts. "Fran will likely be downgraded to a tropical depression (a system with winds less than 39 mph (63 kmh) later this afternoon," the center said.
A tropical storm warning remained in effect from the North Carolina-Virginia border to Chincoteague, Va. The center said those warnings would likely be discontinued later Friday.

But the storm continued to dump heavy rain, with totals of six to eight inches (15 to 21 km) possible over parts of North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland, West Virginia and Pennsylvania along Fran's path. Isolated tornadoes remained possible over parts of Virginia and North Carolina.

Forecasters also were watching the eighth tropical depression of the season. At 1100, the system's poorly defined center was near latitude 14.1 north and longitude 56.2 west, or about 310 miles (500 km) east of the central less Antilles.
The depression was moving west near 13 mph (20 kmh).
Forecasters said the depression could become Tropical Storm Hortense in the next 24 to 36 hours.
